name: LongBench

task_type_en: Long-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, code completion

intro_en: LongBench is the first bilingual, multitask benchmark for long-context understanding. It contains 21 datasets and 4,750 test examples across single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, with 14 English tasks, five Chinese tasks, and two code tasks. Every record follows a unified input/context/answers schema, automatic evaluation uses task-specific F1, ROUGE-L, accuracy, or edit similarity, and LongBench-E provides a more uniform length distribution.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2308.14508, ACL 2024 Long Paper 172, and the official THUDM/LongBench task construction, prompt, prediction, and metric files. LongBench draws from existing validation or test splits; directly converts several QA and summarization datasets with ZeroSCROLLS-style templates; builds multi-document QA from answer evidence plus distractors; has PhD and master's students author MultiFieldQA pairs; constructs few-shot inputs from training demonstrations plus validation queries; creates Wikipedia/C4 retrieval and counting tasks using GPT-3.5-Turbo summaries; and samples LCC plus RepoBench-P XF-F Oracle-Filled code completion. The unified release has input, context, answers, length, dataset, language, all_classes, and _id fields and totals 21 datasets / 4,750 examples: 14 English, five Chinese, and two code tasks. LongBench-E samples 13 eligible datasets into 0–4k, 4–8k, and 8k+ bins up to 100 each. Official inference uses task-specific zero-shot templates and, when necessary, removes the middle while preserving the first and last halves; evaluation selects QA F1, ROUGE-L, classification or retrieval accuracy, or code edit similarity.
